hook.text: A word processor does three things at once. It shows your text, reads your keys, and checks your spelling.

one.text: It does not need three processes. One process runs three threads.

def.text: A thread is a path of execution inside a process.

share.text: The threads share the process's code, its data, its heap, and its open files.

own.text: But each thread has its own program counter, its own registers, and its own stack.

why.text: So threads are cheap to create and to switch, they share data for free, and the screen stays responsive while another thread works.

pth.text: In C, pthread create starts a new thread running a function. pthread join waits for it to finish.

concQ.text: Concurrency and parallelism sound alike. They are not.

conc.text: On one core, threads take turns. Each makes progress, but only one runs at any instant. That is concurrency.

par.text: With two cores, two threads really run at the same moment. That is parallelism.

amQ.text: So more cores means more speed? Only for the part that can be split.

am1.text: Say a quarter of the job must run serially. With two cores, the other three quarters are shared. The time drops to zero point six two five. A speedup of one point six.

am2.text: Add cores forever, and the parallel part shrinks towards nothing. The serial quarter stays. The speedup can never pass one over S. Here, four.

kinds.text: User threads are managed by a library. Kernel threads are what the OS schedules.

m1.text: Many to one: all user threads share one kernel thread. If one blocks, they all stop.

m2.text: One to one: each user thread gets its own kernel thread. Linux and Windows do this.

m3.text: Many to many: user threads share a sufficient number of kernel threads.

race.text: Sharing has a price. counter plus plus looks like one step. It is three: load, add, store.

race2.text: Two threads both load zero. Both add one. Both store one. It should be two.

race3.text: One update is lost. That is a race condition, and chapter six fixes it.

ex1.text: Threads share code, data and files.

ex2.text: Each has its own registers, P C and stack.

ex3.text: One core is concurrency; many cores is parallelism.

ex4.text: Amdahl: the serial part limits the speedup.
